text: Before you use the dashboard, identify the conditions inside the pot.
title: Start inside the pot

text: What do the roots need?
title: What do roots need?

text: The pot contains solid material, water, and air. The solid material around the roots is the substrate. Coco and stone wool are examples of substrates.
title: Substrate, water and air

text: There are spaces between the solid parts. These spaces contain water or air. Roots need water and oxygen.
title: Spaces hold water or air

text: More water does not always improve conditions for the roots. The substrate must hold water and let excess water drain. Air must also return to some of the spaces.
title: Hold water. Drain excess. Allow air.

text: Look at the spare container. Water enters the substrate. Some water stays in the substrate. Other water drains into the tray.
title: Follow the water

text: The amount of water then decreases. The plant uses some water. Evaporation and drainage also remove water.
title: Three ways water leaves

text: A decrease in water content does not show only the water that the plant used.
title: Water loss has several causes

text: This pot stays very wet. The leaves look unhealthy. Does this mean that you must add more water?
title: Very wet: add more water?

text: Choose one answer. Add more water immediately. Or do a check to find the cause first.
title: Choose the next action

text: Do a check first.
title: Check the cause first

text: Different problems can cause similar symptoms. The graph gives useful information. It does not identify every problem in the roots.
title: One symptom can have several causes

text: Crop steering means control of conditions to influence crop growth. These lessons explain irrigation. Irrigation supplies water to the crop.
title: Irrigation supplies water

text: The important irrigation settings control the time and quantity of each water delivery. The interval between deliveries is also important. Light, temperature, and humidity change the demand for water.
title: Delivery settings and water demand

text: Later lessons explain vegetative steering and generative steering. These are directions of crop management. They do not guarantee a specific yield. Maximum drying is not the objective. The roots must continue to function correctly.
title: Steering must support working roots

text: A sensor measures conditions at a specific location. One sensor does not measure every pot. A satisfactory reading does not prove that every dripper is clear.
title: A probe measures one location

text: Use sensor readings with equipment checks and crop observations.
title: Use three kinds of evidence

text: The demo lets you learn the software without operation of a real pump. You do not need all the equipment to use the demo. For a new irrigation system, start with one zone.
title: Learn in the demo

labels: New system: start with one zone

text: Point to the solid material in the drawing. Point to the water. Point to the air. Give one example of information that the sensor cannot supply.
title: Point to solids, water and air
